decisions.reason: The source defines visual traits for the characters, not the appearance or shot-to-shot continuity of the sets.

The consistency rule remains valid unchanged; the source refines the character-specific target style already represented by the source Requirement rather than modifying the general obligation to prevent stylistic drift.
Character style traits do not change the resolution or quality standard for set images or the permission to generate replacement sets.
The source changes character rendering style but does not alter the CC1 shot distances, image-pair structure, character allocation, or unresolved distant framing.
The requested rougher and darker character style does not necessarily change the independent requirement to restore character shadows while preserving other frame elements.
The character style refinement does not change which bridges must be retained or removed in the affected Q frames.
The source refines character appearance without changing animation as the primary output medium or its priority over the fallback.
The character-specific style target does not modify the general acceptance condition that the animation produce acceptable results.
The source does not change the fallback format, its activation conditions, or the precedence of attempting animation first.
The character style refinement neither changes the content of the opening aerial establishing shot nor its deferred lifecycle status.
